label: August 10–16
title: “Yet Will I Trust in Him” —  Job 1–3; 12–14; 19; 21–24; 38

items.text: It is natural to wonder why bad things happen to good people. The book of Job explores these questions, teaching that even when faith is questioned and tested, it need not be completely abandoned. Questions can coexist with faith, and through it all, we can say, “Yet will I trust in him.”

The opening chapters of Job emphasize Satan’s role as an adversary. As we ponder why we remain faithful to God, we should consider the eternal danger of obeying the Lord solely for superficial reasons, rather than for genuine love and devotion.

Job’s friends suggested God was punishing him. However, Job knew God well enough to keep trusting. What do you know about God that helps you face challenges? Remember His eternal love and His plan for us.

Sometimes we learn the most important truths during our most difficult times. Ponder the trials Job described and the truths he proclaimed. How do you know that your Redeemer lives? What difference does this knowledge make in your life?

Singing or listening to hymns about Jesus Christ can express our feelings of devotion. Consider the words that express your feelings about Him, especially as you navigate personal trials and seek His redeeming power.

In the restored gospel, we have truths that can help us make sense of adversity and suffering. Consider the plan of salvation and how Heavenly Father’s purposes can refine us, like gold tried in a furnace.

Job repeatedly asked God why he had to suffer so much. The Lord did not give a clear reason, but taught an important message about His perspective. God’s perspective is vastly greater than ours; His creations and mighty works reveal His power.

When we look at God’s creations and His mighty works, we can learn to think differently about Him and our own trials. His infinite power and wisdom offer comfort and hope, even in the midst of suffering.

The book of Job teaches that even when we face immense suffering and have many questions, we can maintain our integrity and faith in Jesus Christ. Our trust in Him can remain steadfast, even when we don’t have all the answers.

The Lord spoke to Job about some of His creations and other mighty works. These things help us understand God’s infinite power and wisdom, encouraging us to view our trials through His eternal perspective.
